title: Playing on excursion trains
summary: Chartered excursion trains to Jackson, Vicksburg and Natchez had the band playing all night in the baggage car.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Yeah, we've done that in many years. And then not only that, I got a lot of experience on these excursions. I don't know if you've ever seen that.
Is that on boats or trains?
On the train. I never did see a band on a train. I never did see a band on a train.

Well we would get on the train and we would leave here going to like Jackson. We'd go to Vicksburg, we'd go to Natchez. Sometime we'd go to Vida, you'd go to New Road, a different part. That train would leave and sometime we'd leave out here with 13 or 14 coaches. You understand?
And you all played on the train during the trip?

All the way. And we'd get in the baggage car. Yeah. And they'd have beer and coffers and sandwiches. And we'd start playing and that train was rolling and we'd be in there and rocking and rolling with them instruments. But what we would do, we would put on a brass band style. We'd take a snare drum and a bass drum. We wouldn't get no tribe drum. The little fellas could see they could rock with the train. And they'd be beating in there and rocking and we'd be blowing them horns. And when people wanted something to drink, they'd start walking them coaches. Come and get something to drink and something to eat and they'd come in the baggage car and we'd play. Any room for dancing up there? Well, they would dance and walk out the coach, something coming in and get them up there. And walk from coach to coach. Yeah. And I mean, it was plenty of good times. Yeah. Plenty of good times. We'd play every step until we'd get where we'd going. And if we'd leave here at 12 o'clock at night or 12 o'clock, we'd play until we'd get to Natchez or Vicksburg or Jackson or wherever we was going. Then they'd sleep that night. Nobody slept. We had took them for a Chicago excursion out of here with bands. Then they had played on the boats, making them trips. The fellas played on the boats, you know.
This on the train, were you hired to play on the train? We was hired.
They were chartered the train, the organization. See, they were chartered the train. And they would give it for a profit. And they'd give an excursion and make a round trip kind of reasonable.
So you were getting paid for the train on the train?

We were getting paid on the train. So probably you could rent the whole train at that time for $500. And get a crew, you know. And the coaches could pull. And they'd have all them coaches there, well, they would make their money. So you'd take a two and a half round trip, if you've got 13 or 14 coaches, well, you'd just begin to come. So they could afford to pay a band, the band was drawn. Then we'd get at the station before the excursion leave out, we would play at the station. And that Sunday before, they said that if the scurrying was going on a Sunday, or maybe this Sunday, we would get on the truck. And we would play from corner to corner and throw our hand bells. So let them know that they scurrying going. And everybody would get a band and they'd see they scurrying going, that'd make them get ready a week ahead of time. Then they'd have posters on them. And the people, they'd see they had a band, they'd say, well, I want to get on that. I like this band. They want to make that trip, so, so forth. And they know it's music, they know it's going to be a good time and pleasure. So they'd always get together. And they'd make a trip. Some had their homes up there, some didn't go to somebody else. Had a home up there, some didn't know nobody. They'd come up there and make friends, walk around. But it was a pleasure just to be on that trip.
